APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING
  OF JANUARY 28, 2020

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:06 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – absent
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Jerry Velasco, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  SPECIALLY ADDED AGENDA ITEM:

  4.6  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(1) – Conference with Legal Counsel to Discuss Matter of
  Anticipated Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  Item 14.4 has been pulled.

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  4-0 (Councilmember Ancona absent)

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.6.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:08 pm. Councilmember Ancona joined the City Council in Closed

Session at 6:20 pm. Councilmember Ancona participated in all Closed Session
Items with the exception of Item 4.4.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting

Break at 7:36 pm
Back at 7:37 pm

  Gabriel Ramirez – I just want to make a question to the City Attorney if I may I am going
  to addressing the Body as well. At the last meeting I know there was a violation of the
  Brown Act and under the First Amendment is there a way to add minutes to it because I
  was interrupted. I was basically going to abide by the rules of the City Council and I will
  make the definition there is no threats or anything or provocation of it. I don’t know if the
  legal can give me an answer to that question that is something that I felt last meeting
  was unjustice. I just want to make sure that again I will address it to those comments
  that last meeting was very unacceptable by an elected official by the Mayor I just want to
  make sure to clarify to the general that this is just stating facts and stating the sources as
  the California Fair Political Commission. I want the public to know of what is happening
  within our City this is not just personal attack this is remind that we need representation
  not just for the few I am talking for everyone no matter what political differences or
  personals or not personals this has not been transparency and I really hope we really
  have real transparency and I know I see in Councilwoman Martinez Muela and Ancona
  keep up the good work.

  El Monte Union High School Board of Trustees – Florencio Briones – We are here
  representing the El Monte Union High School District tonight to thank you the City
  Council for your support of the High School Football Team all the support that you gave
  not only to our team but the school and the community. When the team made it to the
  State Championship in December the outpouring of support was immediate and we were
  extremely grateful for that support. As you all know the El Monte High School Football
  team won their first State Title.

  Maria Morgan – As President Briones said we want to thank you, I want to personally
  thank you for supporting our football team. I would also like to thank you so much for
  planning the parade for our boys and our families and asking us to partner with all of you
  it was a really great treat that the City was leading this event.

  Ricardo Padilla – I wanted to come in person and express my gratitude for what you did
  for so many of our families and so many of our kids. It had not been done since 1930s
  and so I said I had to come in person and thank the City Council and let them know how
  grateful not only I am but my colleagues, Mr. David Diaz, our Superintendent, Mr. Carlos
  Salcedo. It is just awesome to have the media come out here and portray El Monte in a
  positive light it was very refreshing.

  Cosme Jimenez – At the last Council meeting you made a few comments that you don’t
  have a problem with your colleagues and that you show respect to them. That is at
  times but it need to be you show respect to them when they agree with you then you
  show respect but when they don’t agree you should also show respect and control to
  them and work with them that is what democracy is all about. Your conditions if they
  don’t challenge you if they agree with you then everything is fine and it should be that
  way. I know that you have a lot to learn as a Mayor not because I say it but because I
  see it I have been around for a long time. Not to criticize you or whatever I am not here
  for that. To give you a couple of examples Mr. Bart Patel and ex-councilmember Norma
  Macias did not agree with you have of time so there were disagreements.
  Councilwoman Martinez right now voted against marijuana and I guess she lost some
  points with you because she voted against it. Nothing’s wrong they have to agree, they
  have to disagree.

  18A.  Mayor Quintero

  There is a request because of the late hour to continue this to the next meeting
  and if it is okay with you if you can post this online. And ultimately if this Council
  decides the voters to consider a charter city a charter would have to be drafted
  and put before the voters at some time. I wish since Mr. Ramirez mentioned the
  grassroots we could theoretically create a system in the City which we have
  never done before whereby we require individuals running for office to raise
  funds from residents.

  18A.1 Update Regarding Charter City, City Council Expansion and District
  Elections.

  Gabriel Ramirez – I would recommend to the City Council that Charter Cities is
  not a viable solution unless if you have a body of the Council that are
  transparency it does may work but if you don’t have that it has its negatives and
  the positives. Basically here in this City it would not work in Charter Cities in
  other cities they do either because they have a body of transparency of a full
  body. Secondly, I know the City Council expansion, I am not for City Council
  expansion here in the City we are not like Oakland or Los Angeles or any other
  cities that have a major population that I understand why. Again, not only will it
  affect it doesn’t make an impact for City Council expansion it creates if it is a
  regime that influences others to encourage to expansion that is not under their
  terms. We are not physically ready or mentally ready for Council expansion. As
  far as District elections I am really for it and I have said it before and district
  elections have to be in a very independent transparent not one elected official
  involved or influenced and I tell you this because it can create a lot of confusion
  but it creates a negative impact in the community and it is not benefit for the
  community.

  18A.2 Update Regarding Campaign Finance.

  Gabriel Ramirez – I am actually for it but the problem is that there are
  contradictions with certain elected officials here in this body on the dais. In the
  460s you see money that has been contributed from companies that have
  services and how can you want to implement a campaign finance when you have
  elected officials receiving money from different services that we have. A real
  campaign finance is a real grassroots and I mean grassroots as in candidates
  that does not accept from corporations from contracts with the City like trashcan
  services, companies like tech companies but etc. from developers. Again if you
  are going to make this bold statement about campaign finance make sure that
  you are not receiving from them.

  18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Morales

  I wanted to mention this earlier during our presentation and the plaque
  presentation that was provided to the City Council by the El Monte Union High
  School Board we did not publicly thank our Chief, our Police Department, our

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 28, 2020

  City Manager, our Management Team for frankly coordinating such a wonderful
  event for our young men in celebrating that great achievement. That was the
  start of a collaboration with the El Monte Union High School District. We had
  mention it in the past early on that we wanted to make sure that we collaborated
  with other governing bodies within the City and I thought that was a great
  opportunity for us to do that. With that said I hope that we continue to discuss
  how we could collaborate with the High School District and the City School
  Districts as well.

  18B.1 City-Sponsored Bus Passes for K-12 Students.

  The L.A. County Board of Supervisors has expanded a program where they are
  providing public transportation, free public transportation for their students given
  that they are an open district. Often times you have students traveling from one
  particular regional area to a school that is not necessarily close enough and often
  times parents are driving them to particular schools or having to take public
  transit and often times that can be an ownorest cost to low income communities
  so what I am hoping we can do is that I am asking staff to take a look at our
  trolley system and perhaps consider a trolley to class program where we can
  consider what the cost would be of providing the subsidy for our students so if
  they are using the trolley system they could commute from their home to their
  campus so that they are not necessarily adding to their travel costs whether it is
  a high school or a middle school so that they are not necessarily adding to their
  travel costs. Whether it is 50 cents or a dollar if you consider the cost that times
  five and if you consider the cost if it was more than one student I am hoping that
  we can take a long and that we can do a quick analysis of that and see if that is
  something that we could consider provided that L.A. County is giving us great
  leadership in that. The other thing I wanted to mention, Supervisor Hilda Solis
  has demonstrated great leadership last week Councilmember Velasco and I were
  with her at the Homeless Count we had an opportunity to get to hear James
  Edward Olmos who spoke about his involvement with making sure that there is
  attention being placed on this particular issue what was important or what I noted
  was the fact that she highlighted that this is a regional problem this is not
  necessarily just a problem for us to solve. This is also a problem that other cities
  are getting involved in, that it has to be done collaboratively, often times we
  discount these human beings and not necessarily focus on their needs. It is a
  complex issue and we are not going to solve it by ourselves. Over the past
  week the use of social media and often times residents do place particular issues
  that do need to be highlighted the GoRequest App we are actually placing it on
  the forefront to make sure that our residents are aware that it is a tool that they
  can use to let staff know it is monitored. If we don’t use that app and highlight
  particular issues that need to be fixed we are not being a part of this solution. I
  just want to say thank you to staff for working so diligently through the week and
  making sure we are ready for our weekly meetings.

18C.  Councilwoman Ancona

  Nothing to share at this time I will wait until next week.

18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  I wanted to add a couple of things that Mayor Pro Tem Morales mentioned. The
